description: Hunting dogs were widely used in ancient societies to track, flush, chase, and sometimes bring down game such as deer, boar, hares, and other animals. Greeks and Romans bred specialized hunting hounds for speed, scent, and endurance, while Celtic, Germanic, Persian, and other peoples also valued strong dogs for hunting across forests, plains, and mountains. Beyond providing food, organized hunts served as training for war, displays of elite status, and important social activities, making skilled hunting dogs valuable companions in both practical and aristocratic life.
